notes.title: Hotfix July 1st - Food Tier Improvements
notes.content:
[p]Hey Vikings,[/p][p]we're back with a new patch, hopefully this addresses a lot of the recent issues you've been encountering.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/9ec1e7275372279d649feeaf5ff4d8ae515d52ab.png"][/img][/p][h3]Food Tier Adjustments[/h3][p]We've been getting consistent feedback and bug reports on the food tier system and we have made some profound adjustments.[/p][p]There was a mix of bugs and some system imbalances. What happened is that the conditions with which villagers checked their food satisfaction were too restrictive.[/p][p]On top of that, villagers would sometimes pick food based on other survival rules, which meant that a lot of opportunities for them to satisfy their food tier were missed. This is no longer the case.[/p][p] [/p][h3]New Food Tier Rules[/h3][p]· Villagers will always prefer to eat food from their tier;[/p][p]· Villagers will check every 2 days to see if they ate food from their tier;[/p][p]· This means that any time they eat food from their tier, a 2 day cooldown will trigger;[/p][p]· This cooldown will be reset every time they eat food from their tier;[/p][p]· This gives a lot of headway to build appropriate food stockpiles;[/p][p]· As long as a food type is produced, there should be no need to micromanage food or play with whitelist rules;[/p][p]· Overall villagers should seem happier and a lot of the food issues should go away;[/p][p]· Removed notification marker from villager food preference complain;[/p][p]· White Cheese has been moved to Tier III;[/p][p]· Forager Pies and Berry Pies have been moved to Tier III;[/p][p] Complain and Issue Overhaul[/p][p]· The food tier issues exposed some other issues with our Complain system;[/p][p]· Villagers will now only complain for critical issues, like not having the right tools, being homeless, dying of hunger etc;[/p][p]· All other smaller issues no long trigger the yellow exclamation mark above their head;[/p][p]· Basically villagers should now report only critical issues, reducing the pressure on the player;[/p][p]· Workers only show complaint messages when they do not have anything else to do;[/p][p][/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/470ebd50c1b380957e57d4cc3a3380aa6d7c7fe7.png"][/img][/p][h3]Improvements and adjustments[/h3][p]· Increased Jotun Blood drop rates for all Draugr types;[/p][p]· AI Pathfinding improvements and optimizations. We continue to solve issues where villagers get stuck, we've already eliminated some nasty cases so you should see fewer and fewer stuck villagers;[/p][p]· Added Cheese Buffs, affecting base stats like STR, DEX, etc;[/p][p]· Re-added Leather Scraps Gloves;[/p][p]· Stews pack more food and cook faster;[/p][p]· Villagers food preferences system adjustments;[/p][p][/p][h3]Fixes[/h3][p]· Fixed a bug causing the Villager Menu UI to freeze when using Japanese, Simplified Chinese or Traditional Chinese Language;[/p][p]· Fixed Armorsmith not receiving defencepoints from being inside the settlement walls;[/p][p]· Fixed a bug causing the Firekeeping task from Builder's Hut to not save and load correctly;[/p][p]· Fixed a bug causing the Task UI to not update correctly for clients after assigning or dismissing a villager from the workstation;[/p][p]· Fixed an issue where the road edges would destroy patches of terrain, previously painted with the Roadmaker and Path Planner tools; [/p][p]· Fixed tasks not appearing correctly for joined clients;[/p][p]· Fixed a bug causing cheese to spoil on the Cheesemaker Aging rack.[/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Major Update Seven: Animal Husbandry
notes.content:
[p]This update brings a rich mix of new features, reworks, and much-needed improvements to level up your village life and gameplay in ASKA! 
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/d911851319bc19e1690c0decfd689d389cc00824.gif"][/img][/p][p]Smolkrs are no longer just your curious forest pals (or aggressive little demons), now you can raise them in the brand-new Smolkr Pen! Even better? You can smilk them for fresh smilk and turn that into delicious aged cheese with the shiny new Cheesemaker. It's weird, it's wonderful, and yes, it’s totally worth it! 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/daa0db7de6a90847325ab59ac140226dafe66ec0.gif"][/img][/p][p]The Happiness System has gotten a full makeover, making your villagers’ moods more dynamic and meaningful. A happier village means a stronger, more resilient one. Meanwhile, hunters have gotten smarter (and a little bolder), so keep an eye out for new risks when sending them out. 
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/a744f80a61d0ba79ed2307241a2be14ee375d25c.gif"][/img][/p][p]Need a new look? Suit up with two brand-new armor sets in the form of Huskarl Armor set and Plate Armor set. One stronger than the other.  We’ve also packed in a bunch of UI upgrades, performance boosts, and bug fixes to make everything feel smoother, faster, and more immersive.[/p][p][/p][h1][u][b]FULL CHANGELOG[/b][/u]  [/h1][h2][b]
New Features and Content[/b][/h2][h3][b]
New building: Smolkr Pen[/b][/h3][p]· Allows players to capture and tame smolkrs;[/p][p]· Smolkrs produce smilk (smolkr milk);[/p][p]· Smolkrs need to be fed by a player or villager;[/p][p]· If both a female and a male smolkr are present in the pen, a baby smolkr will spawn after a while;[/p][p]· Players can set slaughter rules; Villagers will slaughter any smolkr that exceeds the set population limit;[/p][p]· Slaughtered smolkrs give meat and leather scraps;[/p][h3][b]
New Building: Cheesemaker[/b][/h3][p]· Allows the production of cheese using smilk from the new Smolkr Pen[/p][p]· Players and Villagers must first produce Unripe Cheese using smilk and other ingredients[/p][p]· Unripe Cheese needs to be left to age on the Cheesmaker's shelves to make it suitable for eating.[/p][h3][b]
Happiness System Overhaul[/b][/h3][p]· Villagers now have a tier based on their top proficiency.[/p][p]· Tiers have also been assigned to food items;[/p][p]· Higher tier villagers require higher tier food;[/p][p]· Houses now feature a new attribute, "area desireability";[/p][p]· Housing points now refers to interior factors, like furniture;[/p][p]· Area desirability refers to exterior factors, like unpleasant production buildings in the house's range;[/p][p]· Both housing points and area desirability affect villager happiness;[/p][h3][b]
Hunter rework[/b][/h3][p]· The hunter buildings now come with a new task that allows for choice and prioritization;[/p][p]of the prey the hunters will look for;[/p][p]· The hunters will now hunt all the creatures of the first mentioned prey type within all relevant marker ranges, before going to the next one, and so on, skipping the ones that are not marked by the player nor the ones they feel they can't fight yet;[/p][p]· The Hunter House allows the hunters to go for wolves & bears in addition to the usual deer & smolkrs;[/p][p]· The hunters going after dangerous prey will ask players for better equipment and will be reluctant unless sufficiently trained to undertake such a task; [/p][p][/p][h3][b]New Armor Sets: Huskarl and Plate armor [/b][/h3][p]·  The Huskarl set is better than the chainmail set and the Plate armor set is better than the Huskarl set[/p][p]·  The Huskarl set includes helmet, chest, pants, gloves, boots[/p][p]·  The Plate set: chest, pants, gloves (completes the existing heavy metal shoulders and helmets)[/p][p]·  The current armor progression: linen gambeson, leather gambeson, chainmail, huskarl, plate[/p][h3][b]
UI Improvements[/b][/h3][p]· Villagers UI List performance optimizations in Workstation Menu;[/p][p]· Improved Gamepad scroll behavior in UI lists;[/p][p]· Added option to open villager menu from assign page on Gamepad;[/p][p]· Simplified the UI for fire priorities task;[/p][p]· The Bear Den can now be discovered and viewed on maps;[/p][p]· Visual overhaul of icon rendering, making them much more readable and crisp;[/p][h3][b]
Optimizations[/b][/h3][p]· Optimizations for world generation and streaming;[/p][p]· Optimizations for world data saving and loading;[/p][p]· Players should experience improved performance from these changes;[/p][h3][b]
Squashing Those Bugs[/b][/h3][p]· Fixed a bug causing task quantities to not actually change if edited using the input field;[/p][p]· Fixed a bug causing the crawler boss to never spawn again after quitting the game during his encounter without killing him;[/p][p]· Fixed a bug that would break the UI when opening and closing the Tinkerer Table from Workshop's menu;[/p][p]· Fixed a bug causing outpost selection dropdown to not work correctly in some cases;[/p][p]· Fixed a bug causing the settlement resources tab to no longer show any resources;[/p][p]· Fixed an issue with world map tiles being displayed incorrectly around islands;[/p][p]· Fixed an issue with world navigation being reconstructed after loading a saved game;[/p][p]· Fixed a streaming issue for multiplayer clients loading into dynamic spawning points (boats, etc);[/p][p]· Fixed a game loading issue for multiplayer clients getting stuck in the "Preparing world" stage;[/p][p]· Fixed an issue where villagers would get stuck behind cave walls and dying from exposure or hunger/thirst.  [/p][p][/p][h3]ASKA is currently 40% off on Steam right now and until 10 July! [/h3][h3][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1898300/ASKA/"][/dynamiclink][/h3]

notes.title: FEBRUARY MAJOR UPDATE
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/471fdc570724290b7c56a14cb612428013858416.gif[/img]


Hey Vikings, we’re back with our newest update, rejoice!
Our first update for this year is probably one of our most important yet! There has been a lot of feedback from the community about the finite nature of some of our most important resources, namely wood and iron, as trees do not regrow and caves can be depleted. 
Without further ado then - the patch notes! (They’re pretty long, so get comfy!)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/b8ab8f9eb77857444e783b53de7fed5ccd8a8de0.gif[/img]

[h3][b]THIS PATCH IS TREE-LY GOOD[/b][/h3]

[b]Added: Forester Hut and Forester House[/b]

Players can now replant trees using Foresters.
Tree regrowth will be player-driven by way of a new building: the Forester. This new building can be found under the advanced production buildings tab in the build menu and works in a similar way to the farm.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/e2bfcfbee1b06c14ec0723b6ea15d17d9826f90e.gif[/img]

The forester has a series of pots in which you can plant saplings. Planting saplings costs nothing, and you will be prompted to pick the type of tree you'd like to plant. 

Each tree type yields different types of wood. For instance the regular fir yields logs, the small fir grows faster and yields long sticks, and for the birch tree you'll have to upgrade the forester.

Saplings require water and compost to grow, similar to regular crop fields. Once a sapling's growth reaches 100% it can be picked up and planted.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/3216d67cbed736f8c0445b0e73acf28feb5ba32f.gif[/img]

Before you can plant a tree however, you'll need to get yourself a shovel. Shovels are new items which allow you to dig holes where trees can be planted. Once a tree is planted, you'll have to wait for it to grow, but you won't have to tend to it anymore, just let nature take its course. Currently, a fir grows in 32 in-game days, and a small fir in 24 in-game days.

Most importantly, you can assign villagers to plant trees for you. Each Forester comes with a Forestry marker and you can also build additional markers. Be wary however that villagers will attempt to keep a certain distance between trees. They will also plant trees in any holes you dig in marked areas.

[h3][b]COOL VIKINGS DON’T LOOK AT EXPLOSIONS[/b][/h3]
[b]Cave Overhaul and Infinite Iron[/b]
Besides the ability to regrow trees, we're also giving players the ability to regenerate iron and stone in the caves by way of an explosive device. While our Vikings haven't discovered gunpowder quite yet, they will discover however that the cave crawlers have laid weird eggs in the mines. 
These crawler eggs are harvestable with a knife, and will replenish seasonally yielding a regular flow of resources. 

[b]New creepy-crawly resources[/b]
[*]Both the crawlers and the crawler eggs will now have a chance to drop crawler sacks. 
While harmless on their own, the Vikings soon discovered that when put together, fire, jotun blood and crawler sacks cause a powerful explosion, powerful enough to rip through rock, wood and flesh.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/190a670118f985d91bc841f77a41ddb62974c98d.gif[/img]

[*] Besides the sacks, crawler eggs also yield maggots and crawler slime. 
[*] Crawler Maggots are a new food type for which the Vikings have no new recipes yet, so they can be only consumed raw. They can be used as bait however!
[*] Crawler Slime can be used as compost, as the plants seem to enjoy it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/38be9c767757ddee3906d48c2e947873a33cd481.gif[/img]

[b]Cave-ins and explosive sacks[/b]

The explosive sacks are now craftable at the Workshop House. They're ASKA's equivalent of TNT and when detonated in cave corridors specifically, they will cause cave-ins, refreshing the cave walls which can be mined for iron and stone.

[i][b]NOTE:[/b] Explosive sacks won't cause cave-ins in cave rooms.[/i][/b]

This will be a player-only activity, so periodically you'll have to go detonate corridors. Villagers will know to evacuate the blast area when setting off an exploding sack. The sack features a fuse, and you'll have 10 seconds to clear the area before the thing goes off.

While designed to refresh cave corridors, the exploding sack can be used to destroy trees, stone clumps and even enemies! You can also stack up multiple explosive sacks for even greater damage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/0adfdc9d971819107e4bb0082f6ed9713a8bf76e.gif[/img]

[b]Reinforced Cave Entrance[/b]
To support the new resources, we've also added an upgrade for the Cave Entrance, called the Reinforced Cave Entrance. This improved mine entrance features increased storage capacity for iron and stone, while also adding new storage for the crawler resources.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/3ca387adc1942a643fe3b5514c19daafede434a8.gif[/img]

Besides the crawler sacks, you'll also find some icky new maggots and crawler slime.
[*]Maggots are a new food type for which the Vikings have no new recipes yet, so they can be only consumed raw. They can be used as bait however!

notes.title: A word from the devs
notes.content:
[h3]Hey there, I wanted to give a little update on our update.[/h3]

First off, happy 2025! It’s going to be a bright year for ASKA, we’ve got big plans and it’s all thanks to you. I’d like to start by addressing the elephant in the room: the animal respawn bug. This has been fixed and will be part of the next update. The obvious questions have been “why did it take longer?” or “why did the patch go out with seemingly less support on our end?”, as in “why haven't we hotfixed as fast as we've patched other bugs in the past?” Some assumed that it was because we closed shop over the winter holidays, and that's not accurate. The truth is that work has been done during the break, albeit at a different rate.

The way we work is that we always build and fix things in the background and what's being delivered in an update is not the true development state of the game. We sometimes have to stop building and decide what goes into an update. We basically tie everything together, make a build, test and deliver it. After that we "split open" the game again and continue working. While the game is "split open" we can't make updates because everything we touch in the game we also have to close back up and then test.

Because we wanted to continue work ASAP on the big update, we opened up the game right after the update was made live, and because we touched some big, sensitive systems it made it very difficult to quickly close it back up for a hotfix.

Basically we had to make the difficult choice of either delaying a major update or a hotfix. We chose to live with the bug for a while to the benefit of our upcoming update. As expected, we took a bit of a hit, and we didn’t make the decision lightly. Community sentiment affects us directly, and every review, positive or negative, is felt by us directly.

[h3]What's next?[/h3]
The update we've been working on since late last year, which will be coming sooner than hoped, is specifically driven by community feedback, and our bet is that it will be very well received.

Moving forward, 2025's ASKA will be defined by more consistent and vital content updates, dotted by any necessary in-between hotfixes, so major updates will truly feel major. We'll also try to be more present in discussions, because even if we go through the feedback and comments, we don't usually get the time to answer directly. The fact that Paige is our community manager and handles communication has sometimes been mistaken for a lack of community involvement on the dev team’s end. That being said, 2025 will also be our attempt to be a bit more active in community discussions.

The animal respawn bug has been unfortunate and sadly the fix had to be delayed overlong, but very good things are coming to ASKA, you can count on it. On the topic of the roadmap, we have a solid draft and we're doing the final check-ups to make sure it's feasible. So that will be coming soon as well.

It's going to be a big year for ASKA and we hope you'll continue to stick around for the journey, as we've got a lot of work to do yet!

[i]Yours bug-fixingly, 
[h3]Sand Sailor Studio[/h3][/i]

notes.title: August Major Update
notes.content:
Vikings! We’re so thrilled to roll out our first major update for ASKA including the highly requested and anticipated custom world settings. 
Thank you for your patience and support as we’ve been building this system into the game for you as well as some new buildings, features and a whole bunch of fixes & improvements that you’ll see below too. 
We can’t wait to see how you all customise your worlds and look forward to hearing all about them! Remember to share your screenshots in the pinned Screenshot Saturday thread too to get a chance to star on our Twitter!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/cbc9e9cb622bd4723d0b3a36ae0229189febfc0a.gif[/img]

[u][b]Custom World Settings[/b][/u]
We're rolling out the custom world settings, giving you the ability to tweak a variety of world generation settings and giving you more control over how challenging a session is. 
Some of the features covered by the custom game mode include the ability to turn off invasions or intensify them, the ability to increase or decrease monster and animal presence, influence weather events and adjust landscape features. A full list of features can be found below and this is something we are keen to develop further over time, so your feedback on this is invaluable. 

[b]Game Mode selection[/b]
Players will be able to opt between creating a normal or a custom game world when starting a new game.

[b]Custom Game Mode Controls[/b]
[list]
[*] Landscape height
[*] Landscape aspect
[*] Invasion difficulty
[*] Monster biome frequency
[*] Monster population per biome
[*] Structure decay rate
[*] Starting season
[*] Year length
[*] Day length 
[*] Climate
[*] Animals biome frequency (Deer/Smolkr, Wolves and Bears)
[/list]


[u][b]New Features & Buildings[/b][/u]


[b]Outhouse[/b]
Characters will now be able to support your farming efforts by using the new outhouse.
During their leisure time, villagers will visit the outhouse and produce compost. Players will be able to do the same, limited by a buff that prevents overusing the outhouse.
Villagers will also dispose of spoiled food and compost at the outhouse.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/73c81a8ec213a6a0c664480aee7b5c477da92d73.gif[/img]

[b]Beauty Pit[/b]
The Beauty Pit allows players to change their character's appearance whenever they like. This is a Tier Two building and requires carpentry materials, thatch and iron. Give yourself a fresh new look for Summer or grow a beard for Winter perhaps? 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/d64e3a05275b96428223e7e120ece5a3cd3c8f22.gif[/img]

[b]Metal Part Collector[/b]
This structure acts as a recycling bin for metal parts. Villagers will automatically drop their broken metal parts and workshop workers will prioritize reusing them over forging new metal parts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/38a0336c1c755623ced8d72de53ccea9e1fdd794.gif[/img]

[b]New Resource: Compost[/b]
Compost is a new resource used in farming that is produced at the new Outhouse building.

[b]Improved Wall Building System[/b]
Added new variants for the various wall types for different angles. Placing walls will now automatically select the correct wall angle based on the terrain the player is trying to build on.

[b]New Addon: Spiked Walls[/b]
Walls can receive a spiked barricade addon which damages attacking enemies. Turn your defence into offence!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/b65bec0eba1ff29e23266e0bfeb118144eb94769.gif[/img]

[b][u]Multiplayer and Network[/u][/b]
Traffic optimization for positions & rotations

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/cbc9e9cb622bd4723d0b3a36ae0229189febfc0a.gif[/img]

notes.title: ASKA Roadmap Reveal 2024
notes.content:
Vikings! We know you’ve been hotly anticipating our Roadmap and to see the direction of the game and we’re thrilled to share an overview of our first few major updates to ASKA in the months to come. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/e52d2332f0180ded9f11305311bbb1b03b857296.jpg[/img]

To be clear, these aren’t the only updates to the game, just the first few ones we want to share with you at this time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/cbc9e9cb622bd4723d0b3a36ae0229189febfc0a.gif[/img]


[b][h3]Shall we dig into the good stuff then?[/h3][/b]

Update One is something you shouted from the rooftops and we want to know we heard you! 
Some time this August, ASKA will receive World Gen Options. 

You’ll be able to customise many different facets of the game including enemies, gather rates, events, day/night length and more! We hope this will satisfy those of you looking for a peaceful building experience, and also those of you looking for an even harder survival challenge.
In this update we will also be including a couple of new buildings, but you’ll have to tune into the patch notes for that 👀

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/d64e3a05275b96428223e7e120ece5a3cd3c8f22.gif[/img]

Updates Two, Three & Four will be spread out throughout the rest of 2024, and will include a variety of buildings, upgrades, system overhauls and new systems. We’re still cooking so we can’t give you an exhaustive list of what will be ready for each update (yet), but you can look forward to things like new enemies, gathering a raiding party & setting sail as well as some more fun additions to make your villages feel more alive. 
Later in the year we will look to launch what we are dubbing our  “multiplayer” update - where we will look to launch dedicated servers for you all.  We’re also adding an in game chat system so that you can communicate with other players online & create lobbies. 


[h3][b]A Note on Villager AI Improvements[/b][/h3]

One of the most consistent feedback themes we receive from the community concerns AI, especially Villager AI. 

We’re constantly working to make Villager behaviour understandable and consistent, and to give you more ways to engage with them. Our long term goal is to reduce micro-management and make Villager behaviour and intent as transparent as possible. 

Although they sometimes might seem irrational, our Villagers' brains are actually quite complex! And they're doing their best to stay off your back as much as possible and do their jobs as best as they are able.

But that’s no easy task with all they have going on: They know when to eat and what to eat; they must sometimes defy their schedule to make sure the job gets done; they must pick out equipment and get dressed; drop off materials; plan their routes when setting off to gather a variety of resources (and try to not get killed in the process!); they must sometimes engage enemies and sometimes not… and so many other such “thoughts”. 

Our objective is to give you not robots which you have to program yourself, but lively characters that are obviously doing their best to assist you and to see your designs come to completion. ASKA has grown a LOT in the last year and we're in the process of continuing to build on this by reworking key Villager jobs, like the Warehouse and Workshop workers. 

We're always listening, and continue to appreciate your feedback and we finesse this to final quality. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/c3ded52b4d9e06a6eb31be7f2292a62af3d0974e.gif[/img]


[b]To Wrap This Up…[/b]


We’d like to advise this also isn’t an exhaustive list and other things might pop up or slip in too as we keep working, but we hope this gives you all the reassurance that we have been and are continuing to work hard on building on the world of ASKA and delivering updates when we feel they are best ready to be released. We can’t wait to hear what you think so please do leave us some feedback in the forums, in Discord, on our social media. We are listening, and we want to ensure we deliver our vision for the game while taking into consideration any major changes our playerbase are advocating for when we feel it's appropriate.

Finally, if you’re reading all of this and you haven’t yet had the chance to explore the world of ASKA, we’re thrilled to say you can pick it up right now in the Gamescom sale for 20% off until 3 September.


Skal!
Sand Sailor Studios.

A new adventure awaits you on [b]Thursday, November 23rd[/b] when we’ll run the 2nd Multiplayer Closed Beta! We’re aiming to make this the biggest Beta Test to date and are looking to invite up to 500 Vikings!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/c82597650ddbb4c230609c8923fa0b56596651cc.png[/img]
One thing we’ve learned is that our enemies are a bit too hardcore for new players. There’s plenty to kill during medium and late game, but too few weak enemies to help you learn how to fight. This has led us to come up with [u][b]The Wisp[/b][/u].
This is a weak entry-level enemy that haunts the shores of ASKA. The lost souls of dead mariners who refuse to leave this world form these wandering entities. Their bodies are made of driftwood and are kept alive by the blood of the Primal Jotun, which taints this land.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/18227de2c3b79f1312591b46947d5bae3ce81470.jpg[/img]
As our enemies grow stronger and stronger with each build, so rises the need for stronger defenses. Our old wattle fences were in need of an upgrade and so our carpenters have been hard at work preparing the planks for a fresh new line of defenses: the Plank Wall, Tower and Gate. These will allow you to better fortify your villages and turn that shanty camp into a true fortified medieval village!

[h3]New to ASKA?[/h3]
ASKA is a survival tribe builder, meaning that the game largely revolves around commanding and expanding your tribe of Villagers to survive in the harsh wilderness.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/d5931bd7f453edcb5187f208e1e22b54965a2c88.jpg[/img]

[h3]Build, Lead, Grow[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/25aa35c94de128a61e4c07a549b21b588c6dbfd8.jpg[/img]
What separates ASKA from other survival games is the Villager system, the procedural world and the village building mechanics.

ASKA's building system is similar to RTS/City Builders, meaning you have buildings with clearly defined roles that need to be operated by workers. These range from resource harvesting buildings, production buildings to defenses and social structures.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/7777fe3d0c15d3ae23c1231a1b4f9b8de044512d.jpg[/img]
You set up production lines and the endgame is about automation and fulfilling your villagers needs as you move from micro to macro, from second to second crafting and fighting to larger scale planning and expansion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/96876ab4a36c2223314cc7629d1b10d1cb8962ea.jpg[/img]

Do what you like, delegate the rest
The wonderful part about the Villager System is that you can always ask your Villagers to do what you don't feel like doing. Sometimes survival game tasks tend to be tedious, repetitive, grindy - this is exactly where the Villagers step in. 

[list]
[*] Don't like chopping wood? Build a Woodcutter and assign a Villager to do it.
[*] Building takes too long? Have your Villagers do it.
[*] You don't care much about combat? Build walls, towers and rely on Villagers to defend you.
[/list]

These are just some basic examples, but ASKA is here to allow you to play your favorite genre exactly as you want.

notes.title: Dev Log: The World of ASKA
notes.content:
[h3][b]The World of ASKA[/b][/h3]
ASKA is a survival tribe builder where you command AI villagers to help you build a lively Norse settlement. It’s a beautiful and dangerous world and the way you manage to organise your growing village will make all the difference. But a lot of what made ASKA what it is closely tied to our past projects and the many lessons we’ve learned over time. 

In this series, I’ll try to share with you our process and our journey. For that, we have to start from the beginning…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/517d2c3b2aa9f35b970d33c937b1f7b86079a7e4.png[/img]
[b][h3]Why survival? [/h3][/b]
ASKA is our third title as Sand Sailor Studio, and probably the most relevant project to ASKA’s development is Bossgard, our 2nd game, where in the latter stage of the project we came up with the idea of an open-world survival level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/49b4b32c6a2c4aafe77ca02a193712918006dee0.png[/img]

Bossgard was a 5v1 asymmetrical boss-battler. One player would play a boss, and the other 5 would team up as Vikings. The bosses were a bit unorthodox, taking the shape of a huge and evil slice of bread, a plunger, a jackhammer, and the like. We had great fun creating all these characters and we were exploring alternate game modes besides the 5v1 arena fights. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/0c42f5d34a0485c726d297e9ccdc0ad38b8b59ae.png[/img]

We found our models to work pretty well in a 3rd person perspective and wanted to try our hand at making a 3rd person mode. The problem is, arenas would be too small to justify a standalone 3rd person mode. Thus the need for an open (or open-er) world level popped up.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/8b4980dbab071f7719588ffda1825c01d5feef55.png[/img]

We called the level “Jotunheim” and the deal was simple: you would enter a frozen wasteland where your fire would diminish as time went on. You had to explore the land, slay a number of mini-bosses, each of them holding a key to opening the final boss fight.

The level was challenging to explore because the player would have to navigate a constant blizzard and everything was white from the snow. Locating landmarks and building a mind map of the level was key. 

We learned A TON from what was essentially a mini-game, a side adventure to our main game. But we saw so much potential in this game mode, we basically prototyped all the essentials to a survival game: the diminishing resources, the weather, the hostile environment and combat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/4e9e7a85a6e4a1c1a94d27acde1859abe575b8cc.jpg[/img]

At the end of Bossgard’s development we were already tinkering with our next idea and we knew it had to be Boassgard’s survival mode but cranked to the max. 

The first ideation rounds remained very “Bossgard” and it had a very different name. Our studio history was made of sharp low-poly stylized games, so for a while we stayed in the same vein.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/98fc173c0de77e4882731e38ae4d4a88a3785389.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/d334b39a4073a7d607469839d612dbdfaeae77ee.png[/img]

At the same time Cristian, our studio owner and creative director started exploring Unity’s High Definition Render Pipeline, while Hyperg (Răzvan), the studio’s senior and lead programmer, started working on world generation tools.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/f045ec37b6334bf68f197cfdfa4b26d4c1014acc.png[/img]

We’re the kind of team that likes trying out new stuff with each project, we don’t really have a history of doing sequels. Our engineers enjoy building bigger and better tools, and our artists won’t say no to a completely blank canvas, it’s one of the things that keeps us together as a team, we share the same kind of curiosity, but catered to our own professional domains.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/89a954b92a4f0a958bdf8356ca4a564d75085b72.png[/img]

We started looking more and more towards a realistic style, or how we call it, a semi-realistic style. There’s still a strong level of stylization in ASKA. The reasoning behind this choice is the same behind us deciding to go for a procedural world - realistic scope. Our team was under 10 members in size, so we had to make sure we made sustainable decisions. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/6bee552866d6add2e0f5acdb3681c70fb5c32807.jpg[/img]

A semi-realistic style allowed us to keep art pipelines in check and procedural generation takes a lot of weight off level design. Instead of designing “areas”, we’d design habitats and biomes that would then blend together according to world generation rules we would define afterwards.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/b9c6ac138ece84ffdf93cc04b96eb105b3dc75c0.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]The Village[/b][/h3]
So far so good, we knew we wanted to make a survival game, we largely knew how it was going to look, we knew how we would make the world, but the cherry on top was an untapped ambition of ours - strategy games. More importantly, city builders and more importantly - colony sims. We wanted to be able to build intricate and functional settlements that would make full use of this world we were making. We wanted this world to be a functional one above all else and this remains a core principle in ASKA - most of what you see in the world is interactable, usable, harvestable, craftable, refinable. Apart from a few rocks, grass and bushes, the world and its resources are interactable. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/0b7489dbc26ca2b6e6fc692d89bdb5c640e7e26f.jpg[/img]

Geography must really come into play when picking a place to start building your village. Some areas are good for farming, others are good for fishing, hunting, or mining.
What applies to resources, applies to village building as well - everything has to be practical, buildings must be clearly made out of the materials you actually have access to at a given moment during gameplay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/8a478cff341e181c794b443fe1b266dddcabec62.jpg[/img]

A building can’t be held together by iron nails if you don’t have iron. 
A building can’t be made of planks if you don’t have the tools to process wood.
And so on. You want houses made of planks? Find mines, extract iron, smelt it, make blades. This goes for everything.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/0c815c7c8ce620c57435981d138a887c167abe0e.jpg[/img]

You’ll see that the first tiers of buildings in ASKA seem improvised, makeshift - they use extremely raw materials, like unprocessed bits of wood, sticks, bark, rough rope and so on, the kind of materials someone finding themselves in extreme survival conditions might make use of. We’ll dive deeper into architecture and technology trees in future dev logs, but this is the main takeaway - ASKA is about representing realism in key areas. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/5df021a5c446ebfef1f9de613c210c3f21048454.png[/img]

[h3][b]Creative Liberties and Why Vikings?[/b][/h3]
That is not to say we don’t take creative liberties. It doesn’t take long to see that our Vikings are more fantasy Vikings than historical Vikings. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/7777fe3d0c15d3ae23c1231a1b4f9b8de044512d.jpg[/img]

This isn't a lack of understanding of historical facts, we actively chose to go down the fantasy route. We like to think we’re representing Vikings as they saw themselves, or as others saw them, rather. Adventurous, intimidating, impetuous warriors, raiders and pirates that share tall tales and rely on intimidation and a notorious reputation. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/cbd82728e0ef6f68e49b7f91389a259d6f48b57f.jpg[/img]

The tattoos, the bare chests, the leather attire, we are full aware this is not how 9th century Scandinavians looked like, but it’s how the Viking lives in the common imaginarium. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/a270c5c899746c7cba19e905f67e6f80cb52cdc6.jpg[/img]
It also gives us a lot of freedom when designing. I’ll go deeper into the design process in a different dev log, but what I can say is that we always look at historical facts first, afterwhich we “gamify” and “fantasy-fy” our findings.

For instance building materials, or building proportions, these have to cater to the game’s reality. For instance when designing a house, we have to take into account the 3rd person perspective. It’s not just the character going inside the house, it’s the character and the “camera crew” as well. This alters proportions, and everything in ASKA has to answer these challenges.


[h3][b]In Conclusion...[/b][/h3]
That's it for today, remember that you can [url=https://www.twitch.tv/sandsailorstudio]see weekly gameplay of ASKA on our Twitch[/url]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/700ff705bed87f71eafec2319aefa225edd2b62d.png[/img]
This is one of many upcoming devlogs and hopefully it manages to provide you with a wider perspective into the whole creative process behind a game like ASKA.

And if you have any burning questions you can always join our Discord and start the conversation directly with us devs!

[url=https://discord.gg/pRzxd4dKj7][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/fb07349848bae4bb00319fa0f7b0f796a20e5c3e.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: A new character!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/6bee552866d6add2e0f5acdb3681c70fb5c32807.jpg[/img]
[h3]Ragnar's Story[/h3]
Ragnar Son of Bjorn was born to an impoverished and struggling family. Bjorn the Ragbearer, as his father was known, was forced to sell Ragnar and his brother into slavery. Fate lead them to the coal mines of Jarl Gosta of the Splinterlands, where they toiled away for 15 years.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/548272c085a32cdf36a9f24843539493edb86dde.jpg[/img]
[h3]An unlikely hero[/h3]
A violent incident involving the Jarl’s son prompted Ragnar to jump to the young heir’s aid, saving him from a group of hired blades. The Jarl restored Ragnar his freedom as reward, and offered him a position among the Jarl’s Housecarls.

[h3]From thrall to thane[/h3]
Years later, Ragnar finds himself a minor noble, with his own fief and people settled at the border of the Jarl’s territory. His ascension was abruptly cut to a halt soon after a troubling disease made its way among his followers. Troubling reports of the affliction describe a sudden decay of the skin, bubbling pustules, speaking in tongues and irrationally violent demeanour.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/cbd82728e0ef6f68e49b7f91389a259d6f48b57f.jpg[/img]
[h3]A change in the wind[/h3]
Seeing traditional cures fail abhorrently, Ragnar soon became wise to tales of a distant land, where the blood of giants still boils in the earth. Hearing of an expedition being organised by Aska, Ragnar quickly made all the preparations and joined the voyage. Aska was a chieftain of legend who through her adventures secured the sacred Eye of Odin. 

[h3]A new hope in the new world[/h3]
A mythical land, a legendary warrior-woman and an ancient sacred relic seemed to Ragnar to be the best chance he might have of securing a cure and a future for his people.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/7777fe3d0c15d3ae23c1231a1b4f9b8de044512d.jpg[/img]
[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
While the perk system hasn't been fully explored yet in ASKA, our plans are to make each character something akin to a "class". To that end, Ragnar is our first opportunity of giving our characters more character, so they feel more than just "skins".

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/21a80b306a8fb3b24d09dc1e21494d1bccd7796c.jpg[/img]
[list]
[h3]A Workhorse[/h3]
Ragnar is designed to excel at physical labor, especially when it comes to breaking rocks. His past as a miner and his obsession with Jotun Blood have shaped Ragnar into a rock-breaking workhorse.

[h3]Perks[/h3]
[*] Ragnar starts the game [b]with more Strength[/b] than other characters, making him ideal for kickstarting a settlement.
[*] His years in the mines also give him a [b]Stonecutting starting bonus[/b]. A true rocker.
[*] Ragnar’s physical prowess however requires him to[b] consume more food than other characters[/b], making him a bigger strain on the village’s food production.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/b74c77026f184569b1ab850044d15701ed5d685a.jpg[/img]

[h3]About Playable Characters[/h3]
[list]
[*] Characters will be selectable from the main menu when starting a new game.
[*] Each character has its own world, but in the future you’ll be able to join your friends’ multiplayer sessions using any of your existing characters.
[*] At the moment Ragnar is still work-in-progress, we’re still in the process of adding animations and fitting existing equipment to his model.
[/list]
We can’t wait to let you take him for a test drive, as it’s the first time since the start of the project when a character other than Aska is available to play.

[h3]When is the next test?[/h3]
So far we're in the middle of optimizing performance and implementing feedback from our previous Closed Alpha. The merry month of May will most probably be dedicated to this.

[b]By far the most resource intensive aspect of ASKA's development is the multiplayer.[/b] We don't have an estimate at the moment for a first playable, but it will definitely be the star of the show for the Open Beta. You can expect at least one more Closed Beta before committing to an Open Beta date.

Although people draw comparisons to Valheim or Medieval Dynasty, the biggest technical challenge for us remains networking our procedurally generated world, as well as all the AI's that are running around. The compact nature of our team also has an impact in terms of development time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/a7a1955ec59a4910491fcaca3e666d215ffa1dda.png[/img]

The scope of the game is another reason why we've opted to go for a 4-player format for our co-op mode. We'd rather see it stable in a tighter scenario first, as afterwards we'll be in a much better position to discuss things like dedicated servers or higher player numbers, which have been our followers' major concerns in terms of multiplayer.

[h3]The World Grows[/h3]
Work has begun on new biomes as we get closer and closer to a gameplay loop that involves sailing to other islands. We'll have an update dedicated exclusively to the new environments you can expect from ASKA.

[h3]See Ragnar live![/h3]
We’ve been playing a bit with Ragnar during our last Friday stream, make sure [url=https://www.twitch.tv/videos/1805955668]you check out the VOD here.[/url]
You can tune in this Friday as well to see us enjoy some more man-action. [url=https://www.twitch.tv/sandsailorstudio]We do a Dev Stream every Friday.
[/url]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/97e6e5b5f0cf89c972e84a57ff452ca016c1a61a.jpg[/img]

[h3]ASKA on Discord[/h3]
We're very active on Discord and feature a wonderful community as well, make sure you join us there! All the important news are dropped there first, especially Alpha/Beta opportunities.

[url=https://discord.gg/pRzxd4dKj7][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/fb07349848bae4bb00319fa0f7b0f796a20e5c3e.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: Sign Up For The January Closed Alpha!
notes.content:
[h2][b]Hail Tribe Leaders![/b][/h2]
Between the 23rd and 29th of January we’ll be running a Closed Alpha playtest, and here’s everything you need to know if you want to be part of it!

[h2][b]How to sign up?[/b][/h2]
To sign up all you have to do is join our Discord and head over to [b]#closed-alpha-signup[/b]
All the information is contained there. Or if you'd like to find out more right now, keep reading! 

[url=https://discord.gg/pRzxd4dKj7][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/ddbc789b2307289491257c6825780ae93c99b2da.jpg[/img][/url]

[b]Below you can find the complete feature list, content list and conditions for the playtest![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/f5041c5359738c4c2a43e786b9690125cbc91e41.jpg[/img]
[h2][b]What you can play in this version[/b][/h2]
Detailed below is everything contained in this build in terms of features and content.
[list]
[*] A complete survival game, with cold, thirst and hunger. Make a camp, survive the weather, wild animals and undead enemies.
[*] Build a complete, self-reliant Viking village using bushcraft/pre-metal technology. Players will have access to the complete Tier 1 Technology Tree.
[*] Organize and command AI Villagers. Build and furnish their homes, ensure they stay warm and well fed. Give your Villagers jobs, like Woodcutter, Gatherer, Stonecutter, Toolmaker, FIsherman and much more.
[*] Construct Houses, resource gatherers and toolmakers. Your industries are inter-connected, allowing you to automate and optimise your village’s survival.
[*] Hunt, fish and forage for food. Venison, a wide variety of fish species, and a diverse seasonal flora form the basis of your survival.
[*] Fight a variety of undead enemies in skillful stamina-based 3rd person combat. Perform light and heavy attacks, combos, dodges. Includes a complete melee and ranged combat system. Use one handed and two handed weapons, shields, and bow.
[*] Craft a variety of stone tools and weapons, as well as a linen outfit.
[*] Explore old ruins, fight their inhabitants and obtain valuable resources.
[*] Tame wolves and turn them into companion Dogs.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/0a36c4b6e870f32698d716a18e4f7bfaf3185898.jpg[/img]
[b][h2]Feature List[/h2][/b][list][*] Explore a large procedurally generated world, complete with a day/night cycle, realistic weather system and seasonal vegetation.
[*] Chop trees, mine rocks and gather resources from bushes
[*] Craft various tools, weapons and clothing
[*] Make a camp, survive the first nights and slowly build up your settlement
[*] Build camps, houses, production buildings, walls and fences
[*] Gain complex AI Villagers, assign them jobs, houses and make sure they have food.
[*] Villagers talk to you, sharing their issues and asking for help.
[*] Have your Villagers build structures and gather resources.
[*] Organise their schedule, balancing Work, Leisure and Sleep hours to optimise production.
[*] Set up automated production lines for food, resources and tools.
[*] Experience a complete melee and ranged skill-based combat system
[*] Defend against small occasional incursions of Revenants or wild animals. Fight alongside your Villagers.
[*] Hunt wild animals
[*] Fish a wide variety of fish species
[*] Face a variety of undead enemies and wild animals, each with their unique behavior.
[*] Build houses and decorate them with furniture and storage using a grid system.
[*] Flight System - Take the form of a raven and fly anywhere you want
[*] Proficiency System - The more a character does an action, the better they become at it
[*] Tame wolf pups and turn them in Dog companions
[*] Customize clothing with various colors
[*] Contract illnesses and heal them using the appropriate ingredients
[*] Locate and highlight valuable resources with a “detective mode” area search.
[*] Discover and cook a wide variety of seasonal food items.
[*] Discover caverns and mines
[*] Discover enemy-infested ruins
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/71f4a4aa7723b237db65f1f6c93515fb411dabde.png[/img]
[b][h2]Content[/h2][/b]
Below you can see all the things you'll be able to build in this Closed Alpha Build.
[h3][b]Crafting[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*] Stone Axe (one handed & two handed)
[*] Stone Pickaxe (one handed & two handed)
[*] Shortbow & Arrows
[*] Flimsy Shield (1st tier shield)
[*] Flimsy Club (1st tier weapon)
[*] Wooden Hoe (Terraforming Tool)
[*] Wooden Hammer (Building Tool)
[*] Flimsy Outfit (T1 armor: Hood, Shirt, Gloves, Pants)
[*] Stone Knife (Skinning Tool)
[*] Torch
[*] Fishing Rod
[*] Fish Bait (Fish-based, meat-based, veggie-based)
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/4e9e7a85a6e4a1c1a94d27acde1859abe575b8cc.jpg[/img]
[h3]Production Buildings & More[/h3]
[list]
[*] Woodcutter’s Pit
[*] Woodcutter’s Hut
[*] Stonecutter’s Pit
[*] Stonecutter’s Hut
[*] Gatherer’s Pit
[*] Gatherer’s Hut
[*] Peat House (larger housing; allows the player to place furniture)
[*] Flimsy Fence (Tier 1 Fence)
[*] Hedge Wall & Gate(Short/Long Segments)(Tier1 Wall)
[*] Hedge Tower (Short bastion-like fortification)
[*] Watchtower (A tall tower featuring a climbable ladder; provides a vantage point)
[*] Workshop (Villager automated tools & weapons production)
[*] Workshop Addon - Dyer (Color the Flimsy Outfit parts (hood, shirt etc))
[*] Workshop Addon - Weaver (Convert fibers into fabric)
[*] Resource Gathering Markers 
[*] Mine Entrance
[*] Kennel (allows the player to create Dog Companions out of Wolf Pups)
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/a270c5c899746c7cba19e905f67e6f80cb52cdc6.jpg[/img]
[b][h2]Why we are doing this[/h2][/b]
The goal of this playtest is to see early interactions with the game from people that are completely unfamiliar with the project. We want to find out:
[list]
[*] what the flow is, what player instincts kick in and how they approach the game.
[*] what players enjoy or dislike about the game
[*] if they get stuck, bored or get absolutely hooked on a certain aspect of it.
[*] what's intuitive and what isn't. Where our design holds and where it breaks.
[/list]
[b]What we're not particularly interested in is: [/b]
[list]
[*] Minor balance issues
[*] Minor, non-game-breaking bugs 
[/list]
[h2][b]How many players will you be selecting?[/b][/h2]
We’ll be selecting 50 more playtesters to join our existing 50. With each future test we’ll keep adding to that number.

That's it for now, hope to see you on our Discord and in the Alpha!

No worries! You can always watch our Friday streams to see actual gameplay and get answers to your burning questions!

notes.title: ASKA Weekly 12.07.22
notes.content:
[h1]ASKA Weekly[/h1]

[h2]Hail Tribe Leaders![/h2]
Here’s the first ASKA Weekly, first of many to come. These will be updates on what the Sand Sailors are currently working on, the state of the game, work-in-progress content and basically everything ASKA.

[h2]📜Closing Closed Alpha Thoughts[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/32a9ed04e53a1d3a133f5f37cc7fdb14cc8762b2.jpg[/img]
The first order of the day is the Closed Alpha that ended last week. We had 50 playtesters who got their first taste of the game. For us it has been a source of both joy and anxiety, as we’ve never tested the game for such extended periods of time with the same people. But we were happy to see the game was overall well received, of course with a lot of kinks left to iron out. But on a core level, we consider it a success and it emboldened us to carry on to the next chunk of content and to proceed with our development schedule.

And yes, you can pet the dog.

Our Alpha playtesters have also gifted us some wonderful screenshots from their Alpha adventures, so we invite you to take a look at the wonderful things they did.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/e6240939eb33f3145c02e7ea58d25a324ed25bc7.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/f2c15b922d3135a0738915e10fd5225d065a495c.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/238f830ff17803ec41e75625a3ea6d132dd13381.jpg[/img]

[h2]📜Next playtest[/h2]
The biggest question so far has been “when’s the next test?” and the answer to that is early next year. We have a lot of content in the works and depending how we manage to implement it we can come with a clear date. Expect announcements in January-February is all we can say.

[h2]📜Making ASKA bigger [/h2]
As you know, we’re planning on an Early Access release, which means there’s going to be a lot of work especially after launch. To that end we need to make sure ASKA gets the best possible headstart and that people know about us. One way you can help is by following us on our social media accounts, because it helps us break through the algorithm and the noise, so if you haven’t already, please follow us on:

[url=https://twitter.com/ASKAthegame]ASKA Twitter[/url]
or 
[url=https://www.instagram.com/askathegame/]ASKA Instagram[/url]
or
[url=https://www.tiktok.com/@askathegame]ASKA TikTok[/url]

We’ll also use these platforms to showcase your work, like screenshots, videos and maybe in the future things like theories, stories and fan-art.

[h2]📜Development News[/h2]
In terms of how the game is going, here are several major segments being worked on this week:

[h2]📜Under the hood: World generation [/h2]
Making the game world bigger, better, richer. Since the Alpha the world has doubled in size, so we’re constantly expanding it. Our end goal is not to have a large empty world, but to have a fun world that’s dense with content. There’s always the question of “How big is the world, how many SQMs/KMs?”. We don’t know how big the final world will be yet, but it’s less a question of miles/kilometres and more a question of what’s in that world. We can potentially make it as large as we want, but nobody’s going to enjoy a large empty world. The question is of content, what animals, biomes, enemies, ruins, caves, islands populate that world. We have to build a world that’s as big and open as possible in line with the amount of stuff we’re able to put in it. But this will be an ongoing discussion and we’ll get back to it over and over again. For those of you who don’t know, everything worldgen related is [b]Hyperg[/b]’s domain. So if you have questions of how math becomes land, you know where to knock.


[h2]📜Boss Battles [/h2]
This week we’re working on the first big baddie of the game, our first boss battle. This is a boss that should be fightable with the second tier of technology, the metal tier. There are a few boxes we needed to tick, which are:

[h3]Accessibility [/h3]
The first boss needs to be a bit more vanilla than other enemies we have planned. It needs to feel familiar and slightly predictable so we ease the player in the idea of fighting large bastards. 

[h3]Lore[/h3]
To that idea, we came up with [b]“The Forgotten”[/b]. Folk heroes, legendary generals, fabled shieldmaidens, defenders of the defenceless, or champions of the meek - they would all receive a god’s burial, and when the last sliver of flesh would fall off their bones,  a new form would be made for them, one that would not rot, nor wither, so that their service might be eternal. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/5c0244e6a80f68e4fdd57e3115c96217bc20d011.png[/img]
But time showed these people of old the limit of their wit, and even that which never rots, rots still. The rich engravings which adorned the bodies of these eternal heroes faded away, the power which maintained their sanity and soul faded, and age perverted these former beacons of virtue into mindless and violent earth puppets. However, deep in their bones of rock lies a power that animates them still, a power that your tribe could very much put to good use…

The Forgotten is [b]Cristian[/b]’s baby, he made the model and will continue breathing life into the rock behemoth, up to the moment it ends up beating the life out of the player character.


[h2]📜Under the hood: Sailing[/h2]
This week Ionut is in charge of sailing, keeping the Villagers from drowning and having them fish from a boat! We have a nice fishing boat we’ll be showcasing in the near future and everything fish related will get a massive upgrade. For the moment, fishing works by having the Villagers fish from the Fishing Hut’s pontoon. This is valid for Tier 1 (Wood Age) and in Tier 2 (Metal Age) fishermen will be able to go out at sea and fish better fish!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43222048/e7d04dd065063a8269475c49e4e65833e25ee78a.png[/img]

[h2]📜Upcoming: Metalworking Industry[/h2]
Speaking of Metalworking, I’m also working on getting the buildings ready for the metal age. Charcoal making, iron smelting and blacksmithing, these are the buildings currently being under construction and will definitely be part of the next week’s ASKA Weekly.

[h2]📜Stream![/h2]
This Friday we’re getting back to our regular streaming schedule. This week we’re doing something special, we’ll try to boot up the saves from the Closed Alpha and show you a few of the villages our players made. Hopefully we’ll have the “owners” in chat as well to guide us and tell us what’s what. We’ve already shown you some of their work, now we’ll actually step inside their settlements! So tune in!

That’s the end of this ASKA Weekly! Share your thoughts on #aska-discussion!
